text: Use Aimparency as the strategy and intent agent for external autonomous runtimes
description: Aimparency preserves human-governed intent, explains priority context, proposes bounded delegations to independently operated specialist agents, and reconciles returned evidence. MCP remains the local graph-tool boundary; A2A is the peer-agent interoperability boundary. The architecture is specified in meta/a2a-strategy-agent-boundary.md. Implementation is activated only by a qualified customer workflow or a credible deployer agreeing to a concrete exchange, so protocol work does not displace economic validation.
reflection: Researched the official A2A 1.0 specification and repositories and created meta/a2a-strategy-agent-boundary.md. Defined Aimparency's role as the human-intent/strategy agent, separated A2A peer collaboration from MCP graph tooling, mapped three candidate skills, specified bounded delegation and verification rules, and limited the first possible implementation to a generated Agent Card plus one authenticated read-only skill. The document explicitly keeps customer validation ahead of protocol completeness.

supportingConnections.explanation: Smallest protocol-compliant exposure of the strategy-agent architecture.

status.comment: The integration boundary and staged activation criteria are now specified against official A2A 1.0. Awaiting Felix's architectural acceptance; implementation remains deliberately gated on a real interoperability case.
